candidates.title: LAN-exposed Vite proxy permits unauthenticated reads from loopback classroom service
candidates.attacker_controlled_source: An unauthenticated LAN client can send GET /api/fuckseats-proxy?target=<encoded loopback URL> when the documented dev:lan command binds Vite to 0.0.0.0.
candidates.broken_control: The allowlist constrains the outbound destination but does not restrict req.socket.remoteAddress, authenticate the caller, or require a trusted Origin/Host. Thus remote clients inherit the dev host's loopback access.
candidates.sink: http.request connects from the developer host to 127.0.0.1/localhost on port 23948 or 8000 and proxyRes.pipe returns the response to the remote requester.
candidates.impact: A LAN attacker can first read / to enumerate classroom IDs/names/counts, then read /classroom/<id>/state/ to obtain student, seating, score/tag, and workspace data from a loopback-only FuckSeats instance.
candidates.closest_apparent_control: isAllowedFuckSeatsProxyTarget rejects non-HTTP, non-loopback hosts, other ports, queries, and other paths. This prevents arbitrary SSRF but is mis-scoped because it does not enforce that the inbound requester is local.

validation.method: Static source-to-sink trace across package.json, Vite plugin registration, request handler, shared allowlist, and importer data model.
validation.evidence: dev:lan binds publicly; plugin is always registered; handler has no inbound guard before the loopback request; configured root and state paths expose exactly the data consumed by the importer.
validation.not_run: No dev server or local FuckSeats instance was started because this assignment was read-only.

preconditions: A FuckSeats service listens on an allowed loopback port
Attacker can reach TCP 5173 on the same network
steps: Parse returned index to enumerate numeric classroom IDs
Receive the loopback service response through the Vite server
constraints: Production static builds are not affected because configureServer is dev-server-only
Default npm run dev binds to 127.0.0.1; exposure requires the explicit dev:lan workflow

taxonomy.family: unintended proxy / missing authentication / sensitive data exposure

candidates.severity_context: Likely medium when dev:lan is used around real classroom data; otherwise not reachable.

candidates.title: Vitest HTML report inserts unescaped test error fields into innerHTML
candidates.attacker_controlled_source: Test-result metadata supplies error.name/nameStr, error.message, error.stack/stackStr, including results produced by contributor-controlled tests or a modified tracked html.meta.json.gz.
candidates.broken_control: The error-to-HTML helper interpolates name/nameStr without ql() escaping in both ANSI branches and also interpolates message without escaping when only the stack contains ANSI. It then assigns the constructed string to result.htmlError.
candidates.sink: Vue renders result.htmlError through an innerHTML property. The report page has no CSP, so injected event handlers or active markup can execute.
candidates.impact: Script execution in the downloaded/served CI test-report origin can read report contents and origin storage and issue authenticated or local-network browser requests available to the reviewer.
candidates.closest_apparent_control: ql() correctly escapes diff text, console output, and ANSI message/stack data in nearby paths, and task-name highlighting escapes before innerHTML. The vulnerable helper omits the same control for error name and one message branch; ANSI-to-HTML conversion is not an HTML sanitizer.

validation.method: Full-bundle source-to-sink review plus JavaScript syntax validation.
validation.evidence: The static report fetches METADATA_PATH, deserializes test results, constructs htmlError with unescaped fields at offsets 240558/240774, and renders it via innerHTML at offset 242668. The tracked html/ directory is uploaded by CI even when tests fail.
validation.not_run: No crafted report was opened in a browser because this assignment was read-only.

preconditions: Attacker can influence test error metadata, such as through contributor-controlled failing tests or a modified compressed report payload
Reviewer downloads and opens/serves the uploaded html/ artifact
The affected failed test report is rendered
steps: Produce an error whose name/nameStr contains active HTML and whose message or stack contains an ANSI escape sequence
CI uploads the tracked/generated html report because artifact upload uses if: always()
ViewReport builds result.htmlError without escaping the attacker field
Vue assigns it to innerHTML and browser executes active markup
constraints: This is a CI/developer artifact surface, not the production seating-chart UI
GitHub does not render artifact HTML inline; exploitation requires the reviewer to open or locally serve the report

taxonomy.family: stored DOM XSS in generated test report

candidates.severity_context: Low-to-medium due required artifact-opening interaction and non-production scope, with higher impact if served in a trusted developer origin.
